label: QSFP28 100GBASE-FR1 single-lambda 2 km
notes: IEEE 802.3cu Clause 140 (100GBASE-FR1), the 2 km rung of the single-lambda 100G pair: 53.125 GBd PAM4 on one 1310 nm carrier over a 1304.5-1317.5 nm window, duplex LC, FEC required to reach the 2 km. The clause's averages are launch -3.1..+4.0 dBm and receive -7.1..+4.0 dBm, with OMAouter sensitivity -4.5 dBm at BER 2.4e-4 (KP4 FEC gives 1e-12 after decode) and stressed receiver sensitivity -2.5 dBm OMA; Glassforge records the averages, which is what a fibre budget spends - -3.1 minus -7.1 = 4.0 dB of channel insertion loss. Corroboration that these are the class and not one vendor's reading: Coherent/Finisar's FTCE4527E1PxM 800G-DR8+ sheet, which states it 'meets 8 x 100GBASE-FR1 as defined by IEEE P802.3cu', prints launch (min) -3.1 / (max) +4 dBm and average receive (min) -7.1 / (max) +4 dBm, and the 802.3cu D3.x comment resolutions record the move from the draft's -2.9/-6.9 to -3.1/-7.1. WHY THIS ROW CHANGED: it used to carry -2.4 launch, -6.4 receive and +4.5 overload, and its notes claimed those figures matched the clause. They do not - -2.4/-6.4/+4.5 are the 100G Lambda MSA 100G-FR values printed on FS's QSFP28-FR-100G sheet, and a row whose sourceUrl is the clause has to carry the clause. The budget is 4.0 dB either way (-2.4 - -6.4 = -3.1 - -7.1 = 4.0), so no design verdict moved; what was wrong was 0.7 dB of absolute level and an overload point 0.5 dB above the class's own receive ceiling, which is the point the attenuator verdict is sized against. That 4.0 dB is the tightest optical budget in this catalogue (tied with OSFP 800GBASE-FR4) and the row exists to say so: 2 km x 0.35 dB/km = 0.7 dB of fibre, one patch-panel pair adds 0.6 dB, leaving 2.7 dB of spare - under the default 3 dB margin, so a compliant 2 km span reads fail on the default settings and marginal only with the connectors removed (3.3 dB). With 0.6 dB of terminations it never reads ok: 1 km is 0.35 + 0.6 = 0.95 dB and 3.05 dB of spare (marginal), 2 km is 2.7 dB (fail). FR1 is the cheap 2 km class with no reserve - pick 100GBASE-LR1 (6.3 dB) for any span that has to survive a field repair or a spliced repair loop, and do not read a fail here as 'the link is dead'. Lower marginDb to about 1.5 dB if the project genuinely wants to build at the FR1 class. Because it is one carrier at 1310 nm, this row needs none of the 'top LAN-WDM lane' hand-waving the 4-lane 100G rows carry, and the reach verdict still binds at 2 km. Overload is not a trap here: the class's receive maximum +4.0 dBm is also the maximum launch, so a back-to-back pair sits exactly at the receive ceiling and the engine asks for no pad - the check is 'above overload', and a compliant launch is never above it (measured: attenuator null at 0 m, with and without a patch-panel pair). Class figures, not one measured module: replace the row with the module actually purchased before pricing a build.
